outlook.reasons: Distinct: C1 already has posted titles with a single person accountable for a live agent's accuracy and refusal rules (R5303, R9635, R1848) across three employers (D282, D775, D844), hired junior-to-mid, and that accountability persists while the live-watching part is automated (R8782). C3 recurs as one person per department who turns SOPs into agent workflows and prunes them by measured impact (R3379, R4550, R9984, R3287, R3312, R7558); the same bundle appears in sales ops, GTM, HR, legal, finance and IT, which suggests a stable job family even though titles still vary. C4 already exists as Forward Deployed Engineer and AI Engineer (R7764, R8825, R5762), growing (R5399), and absorbs redeployed support engineers (R1642, R8403). Absorbed: C2 is product configuration that stays with CRM admins or moves into C1 (R4295 shrinking, R9416, R5876). C5 is identity and access work for a new kind of identity and lands in IAM and IT governance (R7070, R1437, R8345), with the sponsor duty attached to managers. C9, C10, C11, C12 and C14 keep a human decision (R8449, R9692, R1803, R4431, R6522, R1161) but inside existing titles (buyer, lawyer, software engineer, security analyst, recruiter), while their routine parts automate (R7560, R5057, R7252, R1256, R5423). C13 is an executive and HR planning decision with no dedicated post (R2505, R6160). C15 is a skill every worker gains (R7335, R8444). Automated: most records in C6, C7 and C8 are already marked automated or shrinking (R2791, R1324, R6952, R1762; R3527, R2388, R7722, R1065; R7643, R5812, R2422, R9524). Their remaining human judgment (R8174, R1896, R2515; R6765, R3869; R4593, R6123, R9758) moves into existing accountant, service and senior sales roles rather than holding the bundle together.
